 GOP Senator: Cancel Holiday Break if We Lose 
 Bernie Moreno urges marathon lame-duck push on GOP priorities 
 By 
 Rob Quinn 
 with Newser.AI 
 Posted Oct 16, 2026 5:20 AM CDT 
 Copied 
 Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, speaks before President Donald Trump arrives at a campaign rally at the Covelli Centre in Youngstown, Ohio, Monday, Oct. 12, 2026.   (AP Photo/Gene Puskar) 
 See 1 more photo 
 Thanksgiving in Washington could look a lot different if Republicans lose control of Congress next month. Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio says that if the GOP fails to hold the House and Senate, the party should scrap its holiday recess and stay on Capitol Hill through New Year's Eve to push through a sweeping budget measure packed with GOP priorities, Axios reports. "It'll be the 'Last Supper.' So it'll be a giant reconciliation bill where we take all the Republican priorities that we can get done," Moreno says. "If we lose the House and the Senate, we should be here from Nov. 9 until Dec. 31 with no break at all," he says. "Like, we'll have turkeys here for Thanksgiving."
 Republican leaders are already talking with the House and the White House about what such a package might contain, including funding the government past Dec. 11, boosting defense spending, and raising the debt ceiling. Big-ticket items tied to reconciliation include President Trump's Golden Dome missile defense system and upgrades to the F-35. The debt ceiling will likely be reached next year and Republicans might raise it during the lame-duck session before Democrats gain leverage to demand concessions, Politico reports. "I mean, nobody wants to see a debt default," Moreno says. "That would be 1929 on steroids." 
 Axios notes that however the midterms turn out, a GOP reconciliation bill will likely need the support of Sens. John Cornyn, Thom Tillis, Bill Cassidy, and Mitch McConnell, who will depart the Senate in January, along with Sens. Lisa Murkowski and Susan Collins, who often break with the party. Moreno, unopposed so far to lead the National Republican Senatorial Committee, would be tasked with engineering a Senate comeback in 2028 if his party falls short in the midterms.
